provided.value: Archival optical IFS; 7.5″ × 7.5″ FOV, approximately 0.12″ resolution, 2400 s exposure on August 24, 2019.

evidence.quote: In MUSE, the NFM has a wide wavelength range of $4750\,\AA - 9350\,\AA$ and a field of view (FOV) of $7.5\ensuremath{''} \times 7.5\ensuremath{''}$ with a sampling of 0.0253 arcseconds per pixel.
The angular resolution, obtained from measuring the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of stars in the FOV, is $\sim$0.12$''$ (20 pc).
The data used in this work were taken on August 24, 2019, within the programme ID.0103.B – 0908 (Principal Investigator: K. Jahnke). The total exposure time was 2400 s in a single observation block.

analysis_steps.goal: Prepare and bin the MUSE spectra

method.value: Process the reduced MUSE cube with GIST; mask spaxels and make separate stellar and emission-line Voronoi binnings.

evidence.quote: We used the galaxy IFU spectroscopic tool (`GIST`), version 3.1.0 to process the data cube.
Spatial masking was performed to remove defunct spaxels and those with a signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) below the given threshold before we binned the data.
we therefore used two binnings produced with the Voronoi binning code written by (cite: cappellari2003adaptive).

key_parameters.value: 4750–7000 Å; ignore 5780–6050 Å affected by laser guide stars.

evidence.quote: The input data cube was read using `GIST` and the wavelength range is shortened to $4750\,\r{A}- 7000\,\r{A}$.
Above $7000\,\r{A}$, there is contamination due to strong sky lines, and the range $5780\,\r{A} - 6050\,\r{A}$, which is affected by the laser guide stars was,ignored.

key_parameters.value: Stellar S/N = 50: 426 bins; emission-line S/N = 100: 762 bins.

evidence.quote: We required an ${\rm S/N}=50$ per stellar bin and a total of 426 Voronoi bins were generated.
For the emission line binning, we required an ${\rm S/N}=100$ and in this case, a total of 762 Voronoi bins were generated.

key_parameters.value: Stellar S/N window: 5580–5680 Å; emission binning based on continuum-subtracted [O III] λ5007.

evidence.quote: For the stellar component we computed the median S/N from the rest-frame wavelength range 5580 – 5680 Å, which does not include any strong emission lines.
The emission line or ionised gas binning was made based on a \[O III\] $\lambda$5007 continuum-subtracted image.

key_parameters.value: [O III] image: 10 Å line window minus an equal-width window 50 Å redwards.

evidence.quote: We built the image by integrating the data cube flux in a $10\,\AA$ window centred on the \[O III\] $\lambda$5007 rest-frame wavelength of NGC 4593, and by subtracting the integrated flux in a window of equal width but $50\,\AA$ redwards.

key_parameters.value: Spaxel S/N > 0.1 for emission and > 1.0 for stars; minimum 50 contiguous spaxels.

evidence.quote: We considered spaxels with an S/N greater than 0.1 and 1.0 for the emission line and stellar binning, respectively.
To avoid these spaxels from being accreted into Voronoi bins we modified GIST to consider clusters with a minimum of 50 contiguous spaxels for the binning.

method.value: pPXF full spectral fitting to extract stellar velocity and velocity dispersion.

evidence.quote: We used the penalized pixel-fitting (`pPXF`) method to extract the stellar velocity field and velocity dispersion.

key_parameters.value: Initial dispersion 50 km s^-1; eighth-degree additive Legendre polynomial.

evidence.quote: The initial guess for the velocity dispersion was $\mathrm{50\,km~s^{-1}}$ and the stellar continuum was modelled with an eighth-degree additive Legendre polynomial.

evidence.quote: The code performs a full spectral fitting of each stellar emission bin with a linear combination of template spectral energy distributions widened to match the line-of-sight velocity distribution (LOSVD) of the spectral lines.

key_parameters.value: Use pPXF stellar fit multiplied by a second-order Legendre polynomial for the stellar and AGN continuum.

assumptions.value: [O III] broadening traces kinematically disrupted gas rather than the BLR.

evidence.quote: Hence, any broadening of the \[O III\] line profiles will be associated with kinematically disrupted gas, and not with the BLR.

fitting.value: Fixed theoretical doublet flux ratios; line kinematics tied to [O III].

evidence.quote: We reduced the number of degrees of freedom in the fits by fixing the flux ratios of several doublets to their theoretically estimated values ((cite: storey2000theoretical)), which are listed in Table [1](#table 1).

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust–CO coincidence is partly imposed by the astrometric alignment; it is not an independent registration check.
ALMA morphology alone does not measure molecular inflow or establish an inflow rate.
The methods section prints electron-density units as cm^3, while the discussion gives cm^-3.
The coupling-efficiency lower limit depends on which of the two quoted AGN luminosities is used.
The kinetic-power calculation calls approximately 250 km s^-1 an average dispersion, whereas the kinematic discussion describes it as a maximum.
No uncertainties are reported for density, outflow radius, mass-loss rate or kinetic power.
The distance is rounded differently in the Introduction and Conclusions.
